title: Improved Sample Container Cup for NIRS of Tobacco Smoke Quality Estimation
author: Huo, Li, et al.

steps.title: Store product cigarette packs
steps.instruction: Every 10 or 15 days randomly select six packs of factory‑produced cigarettes (both early‑ and later‑month batches), seal each pack in a plastic bag and store in a refrigerator at –18 °C; keep the packs for a maximum of two years before testing.

steps.title: Prepare industrial standard samples
steps.instruction: For each brand prepare more than 10 batches of industrial standard cigarettes, test nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide contents, have professional investigators evaluate taste and flavor, then seal and store the standard samples at –18 °C.

steps.title: Condition cigarettes and collect smoke particles
steps.instruction: Remove the required batches from the refrigerator, unpack, and place the cigarettes in a conditioned dry box set to 22 ± 1 °C and 60 ± 3 % RH for at least 48 h (GB/T16447‑2004/ISO 3402:1999). After equilibrium select 4080 cigarettes with normal appearance, load them into the RM20H rotary smoking machine (Borgwaldt KC) according to GB/T 19,609‑2004, and collect mainstream smoke using Cambridge filter pads (24 pads per batch, each pad capturing smoke from 20 cigarettes). Promptly scan the pads after collection.

steps.title: Scan filter pads with NIR spectrometer
steps.instruction: Preheat the Bruker MATRIX‑I NIR spectrometer with integrating sphere for 1 h. Scan each Cambridge filter pad over the full wavenumber range 4000 cm⁻¹–12500 cm⁻¹ at 8 cm⁻¹ resolution, acquiring 64 scans per pad and averaging them to obtain the final spectrum.

steps.title: Divide pads for old and new NIR cups
steps.instruction: For each batch (≥6 pads) split the pads into two equal groups; scan one group using the traditional Bruker NIR cup and the other group using the newly designed self‑made NIR cup.

steps.title: Prepare pads for old Bruker NIR cup
steps.instruction: Trim a 2 mm wide edge from the 92 mm diameter Cambridge filter pad so it fits the Bruker cup’s 88 mm quartz bottom. Place the trimmed pad into the cup with the particle‑laden side facing down, position the trimmed edge at the cup top, and press the pad to the bottom with a stamper, keeping the stamper in place during the scan. Discard any pad that does not fully cover the bottom or shows optic leakage. After scanning, clean the quartz bottom with soft cotton.

steps.title: Prepare pads for new self‑made NIR cup
steps.instruction: Using the new cup (outer diameter 97 mm, inner top 92 mm, inner bottom 88 mm, height 50 mm, 1 mm quartz bottom), no edge trimming is needed. Place the 92 mm Cambridge filter pad directly into the cup, align it, and press it to the bottom with the heavier 92 mm stamper that matches the cup diameter. The design prevents the pad from sticking to the quartz and allows easy cleaning after scanning.

steps.title: Preprocess NIR spectra in OPUS
steps.instruction: Import product and standard NIR spectra into OPUS software and apply three preprocessing steps: Savitzky‑Golay smoothing, multiplicative scatter correction (MSC), and first‑order derivative with second‑order polynomial approximation, to reduce baseline drift and noise before similarity calculations.
